newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks rally one percent for aanother record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks rally one percent for aanother record.

text.p: Swiss shares surged one percent to end above 5,200 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) for the first time on Tuesday.
The dollar's rise, a favourable interest rate outlook and firming German stocks led shares higher. Derivative-linked activity and technical factors also sparked buying, traders said.
The SMI added 57.2 points, or 1.11 percent, to 5,207.2. The former record close on May 26 was 5,196.7.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 32.54 points, or 1.0 percent, at 3,291.37.
Total bourse volume reached 2.43 billion francs.
Most-active Novartis registereds gained 41 francs to 1,988. Roche added 170 to 13,035.
Financials were temporarily pressured by profit taking but rebounded towards the end of the session. UBS bearers put on 10 francs to 1,601. CS Group rose 2.25 francs to 186.25.

Insurer Zurich, which has posted sizeable gains in the past few session due to rumours it was close to purchasing U.S. asset manager Scudder, was hit by profit taking. The shares dropped four francs to 534.
Among industrials, Alusuisse were up 39 francs at 1,390 as old spin-off rumours were revived, dealers said.
Nestle edged up 21 francs to 1,809, lifted by coffee prices that fell in early trade.

In the second tier, shares of Swiss steelmaker Von Moos added 1.65 francs, or 10.44 percent, to 17.45. The company said it expects to cut its losses from ordinary activities to 25 million francs in 1997 from 53 million and to break even on the group level by dipping into reserves.
